sentences.en: Hello everybody and welcome back to the Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时会遇到的一些重大生活变动和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目，欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: Now, this one is pretty special because it is kind of almost a part three from a series that we did a couple of weeks ago on how we can make the most out of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 这一期非常特别，因为它几乎可以算是我们几周前做的关于“如何充分利用二十岁”系列节目的第三部分。

sentences.en: And if you've listened to that episode, we briefly discussed why it's important to move to a new city during this decade, whether that is in your home country or abroad.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过那一期，我们简要讨论了为什么在这个十年里搬到一个新城市很重要，无论是在国内还是国外。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I really thought that this topic deserved its own entire episode, especially after so many of you have reached out and let me know your experiences,
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得这个话题值得单独做一整期节目，特别是在你们这么多人联系我，分享你们的经历之后，

sentences.en: what you'd wished you'd known, even the goals that you have to do this yourself.
sentences.zh: 分享你们希望自己早点知道的事情，甚至分享你们想要实现这一目标的愿望。

sentences.en: There were so many lived experiences, but also questions and, you know, questions for advice that I thought we may as well do it separately.
sentences.zh: 大家分享了许多真实的生活经历，也提出了很多问题，你知道的，关于建议的问题，所以我认为我们不如单独做一期。

sentences.en: So today, that is this episode, we are going to be unpacking exactly why we feel the urge to sometimes, I would say, upend our lives and just travel halfway across the globe,
sentences.zh: 所以今天，就是这一期节目，我们将深入剖析为什么我们有时会产生一种冲动，我想说是彻底改变生活，直接搬到地球的另一端，

sentences.en: why there are numerous benefits of this, not just psychologically, but also emotionally and socially.
sentences.zh: 为什么这样做有无数的好处，不仅是在心理上，还有情感和社交层面。

sentences.en: And finally, kind of the big question, which is, how do we do it?
sentences.zh: 最后，是一个大问题，那就是：我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: How can we unlock that potential dream that so many of us share?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能实现那个许多人共同拥有的潜在梦想？

sentences.en: I just want to make a quick disclaimer as well, that I totally understand that this is not always an option for everyone because of financial concerns or passports or family.
sentences.zh: 我也想先做一个简短的免责声明，我完全理解由于财务问题、护照限制或家庭原因，这并不总是每个人的选择。

sentences.en: And I really do appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我对此深表理解。

sentences.en: But for those of us who do have the opportunities to consider this, I wanted to really chat through not just some of
sentences.zh: 但对于那些确实有机会考虑这一点的人，我真的很想聊聊，不仅是关于

sentences.en: the practical advice, but also some of the surprising psychology.
sentences.zh: 一些实用的建议，还有一些令人惊讶的心理学知识。

sentences.en: Like, did you know that there is a literal term for people who cannot stay in one place for too long?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道吗？对于那些不能在一个地方待太久的人，有一个专门的术语。

sentences.en: And there's also, you know, this concept that explains why we kind of get this restless urge in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 还有一个概念可以解释为什么我们在二十多岁时会产生这种不安的冲动。

sentences.en: It's called novelty seeking behavior.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“寻求新奇行为”。

sentences.en: So I think that all of us, including myself, will be very surprised by how much psychology really underpins this very, I would say, quintessential 20 something desire.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们所有人，包括我自己，都会惊讶地发现，心理学在多大程度上支撑着这种非常典型的二十多岁的渴望。

sentences.en: So we're going to discuss all of that and so much more.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将讨论所有这些以及更多内容。

sentences.en: I also want to really discuss and really explore this idea of a six month rule.
sentences.zh: 我还想深入探讨一下“六个月规则”这个想法。

sentences.en: And that essentially says that you need to give any new place you move, whether that is
sentences.zh: 它基本上是说，你需要给你搬到的任何新地方，无论是哪里，

sentences.en: six months, you have to really dedicate six months of time, six months of energy, before you can make any further decisions.
sentences.zh: 六个月的时间，你必须真正投入六个月的时间和精力，然后才能做出任何进一步的决定。

sentences.en: It takes that amount of time to kind of establish a community to find your favorite restaurants and coffee spots to get a lay of the land.

sentences.en: And I think anecdotally, and from my own life, this hypothesis is very, very accurate.
sentences.zh: 我认为从轶事和我的个人生活来看，这个假设是非常非常准确的。

sentences.en: And alongside that, I also really want to explore what are some of the actual behaviors that we can instigate?

sentences.en: It's also a decision that I think personally is incredibly important, something that we should all do at least once in our lives.

除了我们自己，几乎没有需要我们负责的人。

sentences.en: And we're kind of left with a bit of a blank canvas, a bit of open space and a benefit of that, as scary as it can be, is that there is nothing holding us back.
sentences.zh: 这正是追求像搬家这样重大生活改变的时期，不仅无价，而且时机完美，对吧？

sentences.en: There is very little or very few people, I guess, that we are accountable for other than ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们一生中，很少有时刻能真正说这是完美的时机。

sentences.en: And that is exactly the time and the season in which pursuing a big life change like moving is not only invaluable, but actually perfect timing, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为这个重要选择背后还有其他一些心理益处。

sentences.en: There's few times in our lives that I think we can truly say that, that this is perfect timing.
sentences.zh: 搬到一个新城市在很多方面给系统带来了一点冲击。

sentences.en: Of course, there are a few other psychological benefits behind why I think this is an important choice.
sentences.zh: 这成为了我们在这一十年中需要经历的许多必要成长的催化剂。

sentences.en: So moving to a new city provides a bit of a shock to the system in many ways.
sentences.zh: 让我为你们列举其中几点。

sentences.en: And that acts as a catalyst for a lot of the necessary growth we need to go through in this decade.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为在一个新地方感到不舒服的经历，无论持续多久，无疑会让你更了解自己。

sentences.en: So let me lay out a few of these things for you.
sentences.zh: 正如我们常说的，你生活中唯一稳定的关系就是你与自己的关系。

sentences.en: Firstly, I think that experience of being uncomfortable in a new place for however long that lasts undoubtedly gets you to know yourself better.
sentences.zh: 所以建立那种独立、自立和真正内在认知的基石，我认为是非常神圣的。

sentences.en: And as we always say, the only stable relationship in your life is the one you have with yourself.
sentences.zh: 这也反映了心理学家埃里克·埃里克森（Eric Erickson）提到的一个关键里程碑。

sentences.en: So building that foundation of independence, of self-reliance and true inner knowledge, I think that's really sacred.
sentences.zh: 那就是身份与困惑之间的斗争。

sentences.en: It also reflects this really key milestone that the psychologist Eric Erickson spoke about.
sentences.zh: 这是我们每个人在某个阶段都会经历的时期，通常是在二十多岁时，我们必须独自闯荡。

sentences.en: And that is the battle between identity and confusion.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在某种程度上反抗家庭和父母的思想与传统，以形成我们自己的身份。

sentences.en: This is this kind of period, this milestone we all go through at some stage, normally during our 20s, in which we do have to strike out on our own.
sentences.zh: 而一个远离你所知一切的新城市，我认为是实现这一目标的绝佳场所。

sentences.en: And we have to, in some ways, push back against the thinking and the traditions of our families and our parents to form our own identity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个形成你自己身份的绝佳地方。

sentences.en: And a new city, I think miles away from everything you've ever known, is a really great place to do that.
sentences.zh: 其次，它提供了一种挑战，这确实要求我们建立韧性。

sentences.en: It's a really, you know, amazing place to form your own identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为韧性是一个我们谈论不够的概念，但它确实是从挫折中快速恢复的能力。

sentences.en: Secondly, it provides kind of a challenge, which really requires us to build resilience.
sentences.zh: 这对于保持良好的心理强度至关重要。

sentences.en: And I think resilience is this concept that we don't speak about enough, but it's really the ability to recover quickly from setbacks.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们肯定会遇到挫折。

sentences.en: And that's really crucial for maintaining good mental strength.
sentences.zh: 比如签证问题、难以找到租金合理的住处、结交新朋友。

sentences.en: And we are going to encounter setbacks in this scenario.
sentences.zh: 这些经历，这些旅程的一部分，确实令人沮丧，令人烦恼。

sentences.en: Things like visa problems, struggling to find a good place to rent that's not $50 million, making new friends.
sentences.zh: 但每次我们成功克服这些困难时，它都会成为重要的教训和记忆，当未来遇到困难时，我们可以回首反思。

sentences.en: And these experiences, these parts of that journey, they're really frustrating, they're annoying.
sentences.zh: 它提供了事后诸葛亮的视角，即一切都会好起来的，我们实际上已经经历过可以说相当困难的事情，并最终走了出来。

sentences.en: But every time we successfully overcome something like that, it serves as an important lesson and memory that we are able to reflect back on when times are hard in the future.
sentences.zh: 它还促进了我们所说的“成长型思维”与“固定型思维”。

sentences.en: And it provides the hindsight that everything will work out, that we have actually gone through things that are arguably quite difficult and come out on the other side.
sentences.zh: 这里用了很多心理学术语，但拥有成长型思维的人，他们会将成功、智力和能力视为可以通过努力而改变和提升的东西。

sentences.en: It also promotes what we would call a growth mindset versus a fixed mindset.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们作为拥有成长型思维的人遇到失败时，那不是什么可耻的事情。

sentences.en: Coming at you with all the psychology terms here, but someone with a growth mindset, they kind of view things like success and their intelligence
sentences.zh: 那是可以从中学习并加以克服的事情。

sentences.en: and their abilities as capable of change and capable of improvement through effort.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我迷上了我的Whoop。

sentences.en: So when we encounter failure as someone with a growth mindset, that is not something to be ashamed of.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我迷上了我的Whoop。

sentences.en: It is something to be learned from and overcome.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我迷上了我的Whoop。

sentences.en: On the other hand, we have the fixed mindset and someone with that mindset really views things like intelligence, things like success, things like luck as inherently stable
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们有固定型思维模式，持有这种思维模式的人真正地将智力、成功、运气等事物视为本质上稳定的，

sentences.en: and unchangeable and unchangeable over time, meaning that the setbacks and the failures they encounter or the hiccups, they're not something that they can really adapt to.
sentences.zh: 且随着时间推移是不可改变的，这意味着他们遇到的挫折、失败或小插曲，并不是他们真正能够适应的东西。

sentences.en: So there was a study done by the
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学商学院曾做过一项研究，

sentences.en: Stanford Graduate School of Business, and then another one kind of repeating, recreating that study done by the National Institute of Health.
sentences.zh: 随后美国国立卫生研究院又进行了一项类似的研究，旨在重复和重现该项研究。

sentences.en: And both of them really firmly showed that having a growth mindset really boosts our happiness almost in every dimension of life.
sentences.zh: 这两项研究都非常有力地表明，拥有成长型思维模式确实能在几乎生活的每一个维度上提升我们的幸福感。

sentences.en: And it's also something that we can learn when we put ourselves through what we would call adaptable challenges.
sentences.zh: 这也是当我们让自己经历所谓的“适应性挑战”时，可以习得的东西。

sentences.en: So there's no point putting yourself in a situation where you have to fail.
sentences.zh: 所以，把自己置于一个注定会失败的境地是没有意义的。

sentences.en: Like if you signed up for an ultra marathon tomorrow, you know, 200 plus kilometers, that is not an adaptable situation.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你明天报名参加一场超级马拉松，你知道的，超过200公里，那这就不是一种适应性的情况。

sentences.en: Like you're probably not going to be able to complete that run.
sentences.zh: 因为你很可能无法完成那场比赛。

sentences.en: But if you do something smaller, like sign up for a 5k or move to a new city
sentences.zh: 但如果你做一些小一点的事情，比如报名参加5公里跑，或者搬到一个新的城市，

sentences.en: or go on a solo trip by yourself, that is an adaptable situation in which you can teach yourself that you will be successful, that you can overcome things that might go wrong.
sentences.zh: 或者独自去旅行，那这就是一种适应性的情况，在其中你可以教会自己：你将会成功，你能够克服可能出错的事情。

sentences.en: And that really leads to this better attitude in the future.
sentences.zh: 这确实会带来未来更好的心态。

sentences.en: Another element of why I think this is a really invaluable experience for kind of
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们20多岁时测试自我、测试身份和个性的宝贵经历的另一个原因，

sentences.en: testing us in our 20s and testing our identity and our personality is that naturally it really improves our problem-solving skills.
sentences.zh: 是因为它自然而然地提高了我们的解决问题能力。

sentences.en: But also a big move like the one we're talking about, it really spurs self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 而且，像我们谈论的那种重大搬迁，确实会激发自我反思。

sentences.en: One of the biggest theories around self-awareness and self-reflection, it was presented by this psychologist called Duval.
sentences.zh: 关于自我意识和自我反思最伟大的理论之一，是由一位名叫杜瓦尔（Duval）的心理学家提出的。

sentences.en: And what he suggested is that at any given time, we can be self-focused or other-focused.
sentences.zh: 他提出，在任何特定时刻，我们都可以处于“自我关注”或“他人关注”的状态。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time, we're focused on our external environment.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们关注的是外部环境。

sentences.en: What deadlines do we need to meet?
sentences.zh: 我们需要完成什么截止日期？

sentences.en: What do we need to make for dinner?
sentences.zh: 晚餐要做什么？

sentences.en: Which friends do we need to catch up with?
sentences.zh: 需要和哪些朋友叙旧？

sentences.en: All of those kind of mundane things on our to-do list, they really have their place, like they're important for maintaining routine.
sentences.zh: 所有这些待办事项清单上的琐事，它们确实有其存在的意义，比如它们对于维持日常生活很重要。

sentences.en: But what they also do is prevent us from that inward focus that's really crucial and that self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 但它们同时也阻碍了我们进行那种至关重要的内在关注和自我反思。

sentences.en: It's an important question to really ask, you know, when was the last time you really took a second to do a bit of a mental inventory or check around what in your life is
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的问题，真的需要问问自己：你上一次真正花时间对自己的人生进行一番盘点或审视是什么时候？

sentences.en: actually making you happy?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么让你感到快乐？

sentences.en: Who is making you happy?
sentences.zh: 是谁让你感到快乐？

sentences.en: Where is the path you're on now taking you?
sentences.zh: 你现在走的这条路正把你带向何方？

sentences.en: And is that actually where you want to be?
sentences.zh: 那真的是你想去的地方吗？

sentences.en: And maybe there are even some other bigger existential questions you've been avoiding?
sentences.zh: 也许还有一些你一直在回避的更宏大的存在主义问题？

sentences.en: You know, who do I want to be in the next five years?
sentences.zh: 比如，未来五年我想成为什么样的人？

sentences.en: What decisions can I make now that my future self will thank me for?
sentences.zh: 我现在能做出什么决定，让未来的自己感谢我？

sentences.en: If I stay on this path, perhaps one in which I feel a little bit bored or a little bit stagnant, maybe not challenged, is that really going to make me the happiest version of
sentences.zh: 如果我继续走这条路，也许是一条让我感到有点无聊或停滞不前、可能没有挑战性的路，那这真的会让我成为未来最快乐的

sentences.en: myself in the future?
sentences.zh: 自己吗？

sentences.en: And it's those hard questions that I think are almost built into the mental process that we have to undertake before moving.
sentences.zh: 我认为，正是这些难题构成了我们在搬家前必须进行的心理过程。

sentences.en: You know, when we contemplate when we might move to, we really have to take stock of what our vision is moving forward.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们考虑搬到哪里时，我们真的必须审视一下我们未来的愿景是什么。

sentences.en: What are our priorities?
sentences.zh: 我们的优先事项是什么？

sentences.en: What's going to make us truly fulfilled, right?
sentences.zh: 什么会让我们真正感到满足，对吧？

sentences.en: And like, that kind of creates a fork in the road that really shifts your timeline.
sentences.zh: 这就像在人生道路上创造了一个分叉点，真正改变了你的时间线。

sentences.en: And with some of that, you know, a lot of the core elements of your personality and your outlook, because you're about to encounter all of these novel experiences.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是你个性和人生观的许多核心要素，因为你即将遇到所有这些新奇的体验。

sentences.en: And it's those experiences that will shape who you are during this formative decade.
sentences.zh: 正是这些经历将塑造你在这一成长十年中的样子。

sentences.en: And I think the result of that, like I've been saying, is really transformative.
sentences.zh: 正如我一直所说，我认为其结果确实是具有变革性的。

sentences.en: And finally, I think one of the other countless benefits, too many to get into, of moving is that it reinforces that deep philosophy that we have said time and time again.
sentences.zh: 最后，我认为搬家的无数好处之一——多到数不过来——就是它强化了我们反复提到的那种深刻哲学：

sentences.en: Life is not meant to be convenient and comfortable at all times.
sentences.zh: 生活并不意味着时刻都要方便和舒适。

sentences.en: We really grow from discomfort.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是在不适中成长的。

sentences.en: So choosing what's easiest kind of defeats the purpose, right?
sentences.zh: 所以选择最容易的路反而违背了初衷，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, yes, life can be soft and gentle and peaceful.
sentences.zh: 是的，生活可以是柔软、温和且平静的。

sentences.en: But if we don't give ourselves or our minds a challenge every now and then, or provide it with new stimuli and experiences
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不时地不给自己或大脑一点挑战，或者不提供新的刺激和体验，

sentences.en: like adapting to a new environment, we're going to feel a little bit defeated.
sentences.zh: 比如适应新环境，我们就会感到有点挫败。

sentences.en: And at times we see people become really deeply dissatisfied with their lives.
sentences.zh: 有时我们看到人们对自己的生活感到非常深切的不满。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that moving to a new city is going to cure that dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说搬到一个新城市就能治愈这种不满。

sentences.en: That's something we'll talk about a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 这一点我们稍后再谈。

sentences.en: But if that's you right now and you're feeling restless, you're feeling that tingle, that kind of spark to spontaneously
sentences.zh: 但如果你现在就是这样，感到焦躁不安，感到那种想要自发地

sentences.en: leave everything behind, there are a few explanations for this and even more behind why this gut instinct might be the one that you should be paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 抛下一切的冲动，这有几种解释，而且这种直觉可能正是你应该关注的，其背后还有更多原因。

sentences.en: Humans crave new experiences.
sentences.zh: 人类渴望新的体验。

sentences.en: In psychology, it's this phenomenon called novelty seeking or neophilia for those of us who go to almost extremes
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，这被称为“新奇寻求”或“嗜新癖”，对于我们这些为了寻找新体验的刺激，

sentences.en: to find the thrill of new experiences like skydiving or risk taking behavior.
sentences.zh: 比如跳伞或冒险行为，而达到近乎极端程度的人来说更是如此。

sentences.en: Basically, the reasoning is this.
sentences.zh: 基本上，理由是这样的。

sentences.en: New things, new memories, new environments, they're really interesting, but also they release dopamine in our brains.
sentences.zh: 新鲜事物、新的记忆、新的环境，它们确实很有趣，而且它们还会释放我们大脑中的多巴胺。

sentences.en: They make us curious and they encourage us to kind of find out more.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们感到好奇，并鼓励我们去探索更多。

sentences.en: And they also just provide very basic entertainment.
sentences.zh: 它们也仅仅是提供了非常基础的娱乐。

sentences.en: Novel things through all of those kind of elements capture our attention.
sentences.zh: 通过所有这些元素，新奇的事物抓住了我们的注意力。

sentences.en: You are more likely to notice things and be present.
sentences.zh: 你更有可能注意到事物并活在当下。

sentences.en: And what that experience does is it activates different regions of our brain.
sentences.zh: 这种体验的作用是激活我们大脑的不同区域。

sentences.en: And that creates a really positive experience, a positive feeling, which is why there is a connection between wanting some novelty in your
sentences.zh: 这创造了一种非常积极的体验，一种积极的感觉，这就是为什么在生活中想要一些新奇感、

sentences.en: life, wanting something new and happiness.
sentences.zh: 想要新鲜事物与幸福感之间存在联系的原因。

sentences.en: And therefore, that innate drive to seek out new experiences, especially when life starts to feel a little bit boring.
sentences.zh: 因此，那种寻求新体验的内在驱动力，尤其是在生活开始感到有点无聊时，就产生了。

sentences.en: So if you're at that point, maybe what your brain is trying to tell you is we kind of need something new here, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你到了那个阶段，也许你的大脑正试图告诉你：我们需要一些新鲜的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: We need something a little bit different to keep us entertained because we've kind of taken all that we can from what's in our current environment.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一些不同的东西来保持娱乐，因为我们已经从当前的环境中汲取了所有能汲取的东西。

sentences.en: And parts of that might be you need to kind of switch up your routine.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分可能意味着你需要改变一下你的日常习惯。

sentences.en: There are a lot of smaller micro habits that we can bring into our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将许多微小的习惯带入我们的日常生活中。

sentences.en: But a big jump or a change like a new city really kind of provides your brain with all of that and more.
sentences.zh: 但像搬到新城市这样的大跨度改变，确实能为你的大脑提供所有这些以及更多东西。

sentences.en: I think another element as to why a lot of us in our 20s are particularly attracted to the idea of moving overseas or anywhere really is the romance.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们20多岁的人之所以特别被移居海外或任何地方的想法所吸引，另一个因素是浪漫情怀。

sentences.en: And I'm not just talking romance in the lovey-dovey sense, but romance in more of like a literary emotional sense, the romance of a new city
sentences.zh: 我指的不仅仅是那种卿卿我我的浪漫，而是一种更具文学色彩和情感意义的浪漫，即新城市的浪漫，

sentences.en: of, you know, rainy days and new bars and new people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，雨天、新的酒吧和新的人。

sentences.en: We all want that kind of life story that people can ask us about at 80 and we can surprise them with like the time we lived in Canada or we took six months to live in Nepal.
sentences.zh: 我们都想要那种人生故事，当我们在80岁时，人们可以问起，我们可以用诸如“我曾在加拿大生活过”或“我花了六个月住在尼泊尔”这样的经历给他们惊喜。

sentences.en: I think we all have this very idealized glamorous storyline of how we want our life to be and kind of what's more dreamy and in some ways mysterious than,
sentences.zh: 我想我们每个人对自己的生活都有一种非常理想化、充满魅力的剧本，还有什么比在异国他乡学习了解自己，

sentences.en: you know, learning who you are and having all of those coming of age stories in a foreign city.
sentences.zh: 并拥有所有那些成长故事更梦幻、在某种程度上更神秘的呢？

sentences.en: It also really, I think, reflects that drive for adventure, that drive not only for novelty, but also for kind of freshness and risk and unexpected surprises.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也确实反映了那种对冒险的渴望，不仅是对新奇的渴望，也是对新鲜感、风险和意想不到的惊喜的渴望。

sentences.en: You know, humans are storytellers and we want good stories to tell, especially when we're in our 20s and we're kind of young and wild and chaotic and free.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人类是讲故事的人，我们想要好的故事来讲述，尤其是在我们20多岁，年轻、狂野、混乱且自由的时候。

sentences.en: But of course, here is the question we need to ask ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这是我们需要问自己的问题。

sentences.en: Will moving actually make us happier?
sentences.zh: 搬家真的会让我们更快乐吗？

sentences.en: Can we really just get up, shift our lives to a new city and leave all of our problems behind?
sentences.zh: 我们真的可以就这样起身，把生活转移到一个新的城市，然后把所有问题都抛在脑后吗？

sentences.en: And it's so funny because I posted a video about this the other day and one of the comments was someone essentially warning me very kindly that moving wasn't going to
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我前几天发布了一个关于这个话题的视频，其中一条评论是一个人非常友善地警告我，搬家并不会

sentences.en: make me happier and that really what I was expressing was kind of like a compulsion to ignore or avoid my
sentences.zh: 让我更快乐，我所表达的实际上是一种忽视或逃避我的

sentences.en: probleMs. But I think if the issue you're facing is that your life is just a bit boring and you're craving a new beginning.
sentences.zh: 问题的冲动。但我认为，如果你面临的问题仅仅是生活有点无聊，而你渴望一个新的开始，

sentences.en: Moving to a new city isn't a distraction.
sentences.zh: 搬到一个新城市并不是一种分心。

sentences.en: It's part of the solution.
sentences.zh: 它是解决方案的一部分。

sentences.en: Not everything, you know, speaking as someone who runs a psychology podcast needs to kind of be pathologized into being a problem.
sentences.zh: 并不是所有事情，作为一名运营心理学播客的人，我得说，都需要被病理化为一个问题。

sentences.en: Not every desire is a projection of some unhealthy coping mechanism.
sentences.zh: 并非每一个欲望都是某种不健康应对机制的投射。

sentences.en: Sometimes you just want to do something because you want to do it.
sentences.zh: 有时候你只是想做某事，因为你想做。

sentences.en: But returning to that question, will it make us happy?
sentences.zh: 但回到那个问题，它会让我们快乐吗？

sentences.en: There's actually been some research on this.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经有一些关于此的研究了。

sentences.en: As always, science has the answers.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，科学有答案。

sentences.en: And there are really two main schools of thought.
sentences.zh: 确实有两种主要的思想流派。

sentences.en: One school of thought says, yes, moving to a new city is kind of the perfect fresh start that people need to recalibrate their happiness.
sentences.zh: 一个流派说，是的，搬到一个新城市是人们重新校准幸福感所需的完美新起点。

sentences.en: And the other camp, it says that whilst moving might provide us with, you know, a temporary fix, a temporary lift in our mood.
sentences.zh: 而另一个阵营则认为，虽然搬家可能会给我们提供暂时的修复，暂时提升我们的情绪，

sentences.en: In some studies, what they've seen is that our happiness eventually returns to its baseline, you know, before we moved after a little while.
sentences.zh: 但在一些研究中，他们发现我们的幸福感最终会回到基准线，也就是我们搬家前的那样。

sentences.en: So it's hypothesized that when we keep chasing that feeling, we keep craving novelty and newness, sometimes we fall into the trap of never staying one place for long.
sentences.zh: 因此，有人假设，当我们不断追逐那种感觉，不断渴望新奇和新鲜感时，有时我们会陷入永远无法在一个地方长久停留的陷阱。

sentences.en: So these are the people that we would call the serial movers.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人就是我们所说的“连环搬家者”。

sentences.en: That friend of yours who is never in one place for very long, who can never have that commitment to the place they call home.
sentences.zh: 你那个从不在一个地方待太久的朋友，那个永远无法对他们称之为“家”的地方做出承诺的人。

sentences.en: And it's really rare, I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实很少见。

sentences.en: But some therapists have identified that this pattern of behavior, this really frequent serial moving is perhaps a defensive strategy in which we seek external
sentences.zh: 但一些治疗师已经确定，这种行为模式，这种非常频繁的连环搬家，可能是一种防御策略，我们在其中寻求外部

sentences.en: change in our environment to change what is essentially an internal problem.
sentences.zh: 环境的改变，以改变本质上是内部的问题。

sentences.en: So I think it's worth reminding ourselves that no matter how much we move, you do, you know, still take yourself with you.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为值得提醒自己的是，无论我们搬多少次家，你确实还是会带着你自己一起走。

sentences.en: But also, you know, I think my problems would look a lot better with an Aperol spritz in Italy,
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道，我认为如果手里拿着一杯阿佩罗橙光（Aperol Spritz）在意大利，我的问题看起来会好很多，

sentences.en: or, you know, it would be a lot easier to manage when I'm walking in the Swiss Alps, right?
sentences.zh: 或者，当我在瑞士阿尔卑斯山漫步时，管理它们会容易得多，对吧？

sentences.en: What I'm really getting at is that environmental change, it brings perspective, not just distraction.
sentences.zh: 我真正想表达的是，环境的改变带来的是视角，而不仅仅是分心。

sentences.en: So what I want to talk about now is another dimension of this question that we're facing or this urge that we're
sentences.zh: 所以现在我想谈谈我们面临的这个问题的另一个维度，或者我们正在审视的这种冲动，

sentences.en: looking at, which is what are some of the difficulties that we are going to encounter?
sentences.zh: 那就是我们将遇到哪些困难？

sentences.en: Things like fear, things like anxiety, building new community, loneliness, you know, finding your place.
sentences.zh: 比如恐惧、焦虑、建立新的社区、孤独感，你知道，找到你的位置。

sentences.en: I think they all come with the territory.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是随之而来的问题。

sentences.en: It's all something that we're going to encounter.
sentences.zh: 这都是我们将要遇到的事情。

sentences.en: But really what I'm going to outline is my six month rule that I have when I move to a new city.

sentences.en: I think there's rarely a perfect time to make a big life change like choosing to move to a new city.
sentences.zh: 我认为很少有一个完美的时机来做出像选择搬到一个新城市这样的人生重大改变。

sentences.en: And if we're always searching for reasons why we shouldn't do something, you know, maybe you have a partner that you don't want to
sentences.zh: 如果我们总是寻找不应该做某事的理由，你知道，也许你有一个不想抛下或不想进行异地恋的伴侣，

sentences.en: leave behind or do long distance with or a really good group of friends.
sentences.zh: 或者有一群非常好的朋友。

sentences.en: If you're always looking for those reasons, you'll always find that there is something stopping you.
sentences.zh: 如果你总是寻找那些理由，你总会发现有什么东西在阻碍你。

sentences.en: But I think the philosophy that I want us to take, and I'm sure it's a common one, is that you don't want to look back in 50 years
sentences.zh: 但我认为我希望我们采取的哲学，我相信这是一种常见的哲学，就是你不希望在50年后回首往事时，

sentences.en: and realize that you could have had a completely different life if you've just taken a bit of a risk.
sentences.zh: 意识到如果你当初冒一点险，你本可以拥有一个完全不同的人生。

sentences.en: Regret really comes from that dark realization that there is nothing that we can do to change the
sentences.zh: 遗憾其实源于一种深刻的认知，即我们无法改变过去。

sentences.en: paSt. So we really need to act with our future selves in mind when making these decisions.
sentences.zh: 所以，在做这些决定时，我们真的需要考虑到未来的自己。

sentences.en: So although we've spoken about all the benefits, another element of it is that sometimes we can be frozen by fear, kind of almost playing this tug of war with these two desires.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们已经谈到了所有的好处，但另一个因素是，有时我们会被恐惧所冻结，几乎是在这两种欲望之间进行拉锯战。

sentences.en: Do we stay or do we go?
sentences.zh: 我们是留下还是离开？

sentences.en: And there's a lot of things that are underpinning this.
sentences.zh: 这背后有很多原因。

sentences.en: It's very natural to feel anxiety and fear at the precipice of a big life change.
sentences.zh: 在面临重大人生转折点时，感到焦虑和恐惧是非常自然的。

sentences.en: Potentially as well, one that's going to upend one of our core human needs, the need for security.
sentences.zh: 这甚至可能颠覆我们核心的人类需求之一，即对安全感的需求。

sentences.en: And what it often comes down to is that fear of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 而这通常归结为对未知的恐惧。

sentences.en: Humans as a species are really bad at dealing with uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 人类作为一个物种，在处理不确定性方面真的很差劲。

sentences.en: And so we like to create our own hypotheticals or visions of what could come next, kind of in order to provide us
sentences.zh: 所以我们喜欢创造自己的假设或对未来的愿景，以此来给我们提供一种安慰，

sentences.en: with a sense of comfort that we can not only predict the future, but plan for it.
sentences.zh: 让我们觉得不仅能预测未来，还能为之做好规划。

sentences.en: And often these ideas or things that we concoct, they're a lot more negative than what will actually happen in reality.
sentences.zh: 而这些我们编造的想法或事物，往往比现实中会发生的情况要负面得多。

sentences.en: For example, you know, catastrophizing and thinking, well, when I get there, I won't have any friends and I'll be so terribly lonely and I'll never find anyone like me.
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道，灾难化思维，想着：好吧，等我到了那里，我一个朋友都没有，我会非常孤独，永远找不到像我这样的人。

sentences.en: I'll never find community.
sentences.zh: 我永远找不到归属感。

sentences.en: So I should just stay where I am.
sentences.zh: 所以我还是待在原地好了。

sentences.en: In that instance, a negative uncertainty bias is impacting your decision making.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，负面不确定性偏见正在影响你的决策。

sentences.en: And what it's trying to do is scare you out of pushing yourself beyond your comfort zone.
sentences.zh: 它试图吓唬你，让你不敢走出舒适区。

sentences.en: It's kind of ironic how our minds really crave two things at once.
sentences.zh: 我们的头脑同时渴望两样东西，这真是一种讽刺。

sentences.en: They crave the novelty and the new experiences, but also what is comfortable and secure.
sentences.zh: 它们既渴望新鲜感和新体验，又渴望舒适和安全。

sentences.en: But I think by recognizing that your brain is likely to be in that kind of automatic state of negativity bias, you're actually
sentences.zh: 但我认为，通过认识到你的大脑很可能处于那种自动的负面偏见状态，你实际上能够更好地与这些想法保持距离，

sentences.en: better able to distance yourself from those thoughts and think more rationally and also positively, not just about your current situation, but also about the future.
sentences.zh: 从而更理性、更积极地思考，不仅是对你当前的处境，也是对未来。

sentences.en: Additionally, I think major life changes can cause a lot of stress for us, particularly us people who feel a lot more comfortable in a routine.
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为重大的人生变动会给我们带来很大的压力，尤其是对于我们这些在常规生活中感到更自在的人来说。

sentences.en: And even for those who like a little bit of risk, a little bit of trouble, it's still going to present its challenges.
sentences.zh: 即使对于那些喜欢一点风险、一点挑战的人来说，这也依然会带来挑战。

sentences.en: I think what's interesting to note here is that the brain actually tends to deal with all types of stressful, major life changes in the same way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里值得注意的一点是，大脑实际上倾向于以同样的方式处理所有类型的压力重大的生活变动。

sentences.en: So we typically think of certain life events like the death of a family member or graduating university as things that are quite stressful, right?
sentences.zh: 我们通常认为某些生活事件，比如家庭成员去世或大学毕业，是相当有压力的，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are things that we really recognize as being a little bit scary and almost coming with a bit of grief.
sentences.zh: 那些是我们真正意识到有点可怕，甚至伴随着一点悲伤的事情。

sentences.en: But things that are also seemingly positive, like celebrating a new marriage or moving, they can also prompt the brain to react with unease and discomfort.
sentences.zh: 但那些看似积极的事情，比如庆祝新婚或搬家，也会促使大脑产生不安和不适的反应。

sentences.en: That's because these experiences, good or bad, however, we appraise them, they go against our sense of normalcy and the consistency that our brain expects.
sentences.zh: 这是因为这些经历，无论好坏，无论我们如何评估它们，都违背了我们对常态的感知以及大脑所期望的一致性。

sentences.en: So it acts with an alarm, it responds in state of panic, in order to really make sure that we are
sentences.zh: 所以它会发出警报，进入恐慌状态，以确保我们能够处理这种新环境或新体验是否真的构成了威胁。

sentences.en: processing whether this new environment or this new experience actually poses a threat.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这种情况最终会随着时间推移而消失。

sentences.en: Importantly, that is going to go away eventually with time.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始意识到这个新事物、新体验、新情况并没有那么可怕时，它就会消失。

sentences.en: And when we begin to realize that this new thing, this new experience, this new situation, it's not as scary as it needs to be.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我想要引入我之前提到过的“六个月法则”的地方。

sentences.en: And here is really where I want to introduce the idea of the six month rule that I've already spoken on a little bit.

sentences.en: So I've moved a few times in my life, I moved to Canberra from
sentences.zh: 最近一次是从堪培拉搬到了悉尼，我认为这对我的转变要大得多，

sentences.en: Melbourne for university, and then most recently from Canberra to Sydney, which I think was a much more

sentences.en: significant transition for me given I did not have the structure of a college or university environment.
sentences.zh: 如果你听了周二的生活更新，你就会知道未来还有可能进行另一次大搬迁。

sentences.en: And if you listen to my life update on Tuesday, you'll know there is the potential also for another big move in the future.
sentences.zh: 根据经验，我意识到当你搬到一个新地方时，大约需要六个月的时间才能感到安定，

sentences.en: From experience, I've realized that when you move to a new place, it is going to
sentences.zh: 就像适应一份新工作或一段新关系需要几个月一样。

sentences.en: take about six months to feel settled, just like it takes a few months to adjust to a new job or a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 在那最初的六个月里，你不能做任何激进的决定。

sentences.en: And in those first six months, you cannot make any drastic decisions.
sentences.zh: 你不能让自己搬回家。

sentences.zh: 你不能让自己放弃梦想，因为需要那么长的时间才能充分发掘这个新地方的潜力，并真正建立起一些核心需求，

sentences.en: You cannot let yourself almost give up on the dream, because it's going to take that amount of time to fully realize the potential of this new place and actually build
sentences.zh: 比如归属感、安全感、对地方的认同感。

sentences.en: some of those core needs, things like community, things like a sense of security, things like a sense of place.
sentences.zh: 我以个人经验告诉你，这就像时钟一样准。

sentences.en: And let me tell you from personal experience, it is like clockwork.
sentences.zh: 六个月的节点一到，突然间你抬头一看，你会觉得你有可以求助的人，

sentences.en: That six month mark comes around and suddenly you kind of look up and you feel like you have people you can call on,
sentences.zh: 你有常去的地方，公共交通也已经摸透了。

sentences.en: you have your old haunts, the kind of public transport is down pat.

sentences.zh: 让我明确说明这一点。

sentences.en: Let me really state that clearly.

sentences.en: It is very much anecdotal.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这个时间线之所以如此契合这种情况，是因为最初的几个月会感觉非常令人兴奋、浪漫且新奇。

sentences.en: But I think the reason that this timeline fits this situation so well is because the first couple of months are going to feel really exciting and romantic and novel.

sentences.zh: 所以它可能感觉就像一个超长的假期。
